newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND ROUT NZ TO SET UP SERIES WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND ROUT NZ TO SET UP SERIES WIN.

text.p: England were poised to win their one-day cricket international series against New Zealand on Sunday after they bowled the home side out for 153 in the fourth match at Eden Park.

New Zealand made a solid start after being sent in by England to bat first in the match, which was reduced to 43 overs per side by rain. But the English bowlers, in particular off-spinner Robert Croft, soon gained the upper hand.

Openers Nathan Astle and Bryan Young put on 53 for the first wicket, but apart from a 59-run partnership for the third wicket between Astle and Stephen Fleming, there was nothing else of substance in the innings.

Astle made 51 and Fleming 37, but a woeful lack of communication cost New Zealand the wickets of Chris Cairns and Gavin Larsen for two each, and some poor batting under pressure saw the demise of New Zealand in the 39th over.
Offspinner Robert Croft took two wickets in one over and the bowlers were backed up by some excellent fielding.
The last eight wickets fell in the space of 82 balls for the addition of just 40 runs.
England lead the five-match series 2-0, after winning the first two matches and drawing the third in Napier last Wednesday.
